key_insight: Based on the title and partial abstract, VeriCUA treats task-completion verification as active exploration: a verifier seeks evidence rather than judging only the observations it receives.
problem_solved: Determining whether computer-using agents truly completed tasks across desktop, mobile, and web environments is difficult. Vision-language judges see only supplied observations, while program-based checks are constrained by accessible application state.
method: Frame verification as an agentic exploration problem rather than a one-shot judgment.
Actively gather evidence from the digital environment to assess task completion; implementation details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: More reliable verification could improve training-data curation, agent evaluation, and reinforcement-learning feedback. The supplied excerpt does not establish empirical gains.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: fixed-observation judge versus an actively exploring verifier.
Conceptual loop: inspect environment → gather evidence → assess completion.
Desktop, mobile, and browser icons showing the verification challenge across platforms.
Evidence iceberg: visible screenshots above the surface, hidden application state below.
paper_title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
paper_authors: Qiushi Sun, Da Yu, Alexander Knop, Amer Sinha, Lingpeng Kong
